question: Which sectors and regions carry the war and election risk — and is it in the price?
read: VIX is at the 17th percentile while the S&P 500 is +12.7% since 27 Feb. The war shows up in sectors rather than the index: defense vs airlines −12.9%, energy vs the market +2.5%.

question: Is the war an inflation shock (bear steepening) or a growth scare (bull flattening)?
read: The 10-year is +128 bp since 27 Feb with 3m10y +80 bp and 5s30s −54 bp: bear steepening — an inflation and term-premium shock. Breakevens 2.33% and real yields 2.87% split the 10-year.

question: Is stress spreading from the weakest borrowers into the core?
read: High-yield spreads are at the 90th percentile. CCC–BBB moved +185 bp in a month: decompression — stress is concentrated in the weakest credits. EM corporate spreads +23 bp over the same month.

question: How much of the Hormuz disruption is in prompt barrels, products and freight?
read: Brent sits at the 87th percentile and the 3-2-1 crack at the 85th, but OVX is only at the 39th: implied vol is cheap relative to spot, so upside is better owned through calls. Tanker equity (FRO) is +39.1% since the war began.

question: Which commodities carry supply risk from conflict zones, and is gold still a hedge?
read: Gold is −21.9% since the war began and has fallen after 2026 escalations (vol-adjusted −0.78), so it is not working as a war hedge this year. Copper sits at the 96th percentile; wheat is +12.7% since 27 Feb.

question: Who funds the shock and who is the haven?
read: The dollar index is at the 100th percentile; since 27 Feb USD/JPY is +1.3% and USD/CHF +7.1%: the dollar, not the yen or franc, is the haven. Weakest EM currency vs the dollar since the war began: USD/INR (+6.2%).

question: Is the market paying for the tail, and in which asset is protection cheapest?
read: VIX ÷ VIX 3-month is 0.85, in contango — no near-term panic premium. Across assets the cheapest implied vol relative to its own year is GVZ (12th percentile) and the richest MOVE (94th).
